findings.item: Ladybug Tools forum finding, principle 3, flags ('search for AI since Jun 2025 returns 50 topics, none about AI')
findings.issue: This conclusion is false, and the search method caused it: a two-letter 'AI' query returns substring noise. A search for 'MCP' on discourse.ladybug.tools finds 'Ladybug Tools MCP is ready!' (7 May 2026; LoftyTao/ladybug-tools-mcp, GPL-3.0, v1.0.0 Windows only, 4 participants). It also finds 'Honeybee-MCP (beta)' (23 Jan 2026; LoftyTao/Honeybee-MCP, GPL-3.0), and inside that thread idfkit-mcp (EnergyPlus, MIT) and NatLabRockies/openstudio-mcp (no root LICENSE). A third thread, 'The React version of Design Explore' (12 Feb 2026; LoftyTao/design-explorer-react, MIT, 5 participants, runs locally), is an open-source build of the options-board pattern the packet credits to Speckle. Users there praise 'what-if' testing on a resolved model. They complain about token use on EnergyPlus warnings, copy-pasting files into GHPython, and data-sovereignty doubts.
findings.fix: Remove 'none about AI'. Add one finding on the LBT and Honeybee MCPs plus idfkit-mcp as prior art for the energy, carbon and sun modules. Treat GPL-3.0 as arm's-length only: call it as a separate process and never bundle it. Add design-explorer-react (MIT) as the open-source base for the options board in recommendation 10. Rerun forum searches with specific terms (MCP, LLM, Claude, ChatGPT, agent).

findings.item: Principles 4, 13 and 15: McNeel staff statements counted as community voices
findings.issue: In thread 223330, the user who claims '650K to 1M tokens' per render and says McNeel 'would like to connect to as many AI engines as possible' is scottd: Scott Davidson, a McNeel admin. The packet calls him 'one Oct 2026 poster' and counts his roadmap statement as user demand for model-agnostic agents. Staff also take part in every key thread: CallumSykes and Japhy (216568), scottd, Gijs and theoutside (223183), Japhy (216046), scottd and theoutside (211382). The 'door altered' fidelity complaint in principle 15 is about a Krita AI image, not RhinoAI.
findings.fix: Tag every quoted voice as user, vendor staff or plugin author, and exclude staff from n. Restate principle 13 as 'McNeel states intent to add engines; n=3 users moved to Codex'. Attribute the token figure to a McNeel staff anecdote. Move the door example to Krita AI Diffusion, and log Krita AI Diffusion as a missed local renderer to evaluate after 10 Dec.

findings.item: Voice counts in principles 4, 5, 11, 15 and unresolved item 6
findings.issue: The counts come from page-1 fetch summaries and are badly low. Discourse's own participant_count gives: AI-in-CAD 216046 = 42 participants, 100 posts (packet says about 15); Runchat 211382 = 28 participants, 76 posts (packet says 8); Rhino MCP Server 216568 = 30; Claude first try 223183 = 23 (packet says about 18); AI rendered product 219926 = 11. The topic-search tallies also do not reproduce today: Veras 8 since 2025 (packet 12), ComfyUI 13 (14), Krea 3 (4), Midjourney 0 (11). The packet's 'Rhino MCP Server thread (May 2026)' was created on 3 Mar 2026.
findings.fix: Take counts from /t/{id}.json (participant_count, excluding staff), read every page via /t/{id}/posts.json, and record the exact query string, date and result count for each search. Restate each n. Keep the 'signal, hypothesis' labels.

findings.item: Recommendation 6 and the unresolved list (social platforms)
findings.issue: The packet treats Reddit, YouTube and LinkedIn as reachable only by hand. That leaves the 3 Nov log, 13 days away, without a method or a named person. Official, terms-compliant routes exist that are not proxies: the Reddit Data API (registered OAuth app, rate-limited, non-commercial or academic use) and the YouTube Data API v3 commentThreads endpoint (API key). HN Algolia, rechecked today, returns no 2025-26 threads for TestFit, Forma, Hypar or Speckle-as-AEC, so HN cannot fill the gap either.
findings.fix: Name the owner and the backup in recommendation 6. A teammate registers the official Reddit and YouTube API access under their own account and agrees to the terms; the agent must not create the accounts. The team pulls r/Architects, r/rhino, r/Revit and r/computationaldesign search results plus comments on 5 to 10 Forma, TestFit and Veras videos. Use the same template, and record the query, the date and whether each voice is a vendor.

findings.issue: The finding's URL (the release post) describes 7 read tools and no Write installers. The Write and Experimental installers and the Revit 2027.2 requirement come from blog.autodesk.io/revit-mcp-server-update/ (29 Sep 2026). That post advises backing up the project and does not say writes are undoable. 'Undoable' comes only from AEC Magazine quoting an Autodesk executive on 'Trusted Write'.
findings.fix: Cite the update post as the primary source for the installers. Attribute 'undoable' to the AEC Magazine interview and keep the backup advice.

findings.issue: The README says 'npx ctx7 setup' signs the user in through OAuth and generates an API key, and recommends a free key for higher rate limits. Setup therefore creates an account and ties queries to it. The packet says only that free-tier limits are unstated, and the 0.5 h estimate omits the sign-in.
findings.fix: State that a Context7 account and key are required, that each user creates them personally, and that the key goes in an ${ENV} variable. Add this to item 2 of the do-this-first list.

findings.issue: The Claude Code MCP docs list one more silent-load case: a session started in bypassPermissions mode with skipDangerousModePermissionPrompt set. They also say --strict-mcp-config skips approval for unloaded project servers only on v2.1.246 or later. Neither is in the policy.
findings.fix: Add the bypassPermissions case and pin a minimum Claude Code version (at least 2.1.246; 2.1.274 or later for the default v2 MCP runtime) in the project README.

findings.issue: The README quick start installs through the Claude Desktop connector (connector.mcpb) and names no Yak package. A McNeel admin wrote on 8 Oct 2026 that the AI panel is included with the Rhino 9 Beta and currently connects to Claude and Codex. The finding cites forum-only install routes and leaves the Rhino 9 dependency implicit.
findings.fix: Record both install routes, and that the AI panel targets the Rhino 9 Beta. Keep the 'test on the lab's Rhino 8' gate.

findings.issue: The options-board principle rests on one vendor post from a hosted product. An MIT, locally runnable Design Explorer exists (design-explorer-react), and Ladybug forum users raised concrete problems with it: text variables were filtered out, and they doubted where files were uploaded.
findings.fix: Cite design-explorer-react with the vendor post. Turn the user complaints into requirements: keep categorical variables, process locally, and state plainly where data goes.

findings.issue: Thirty findings, ten recommendations and more than thirty flags remain. Rounds 1 and 2 left flags in place after they were superseded (for example, the Figma 'superseded' flag and the Node flag), which adds reading time.
findings.fix: Collapse resolved flags into one line each, and move roadmap-only findings (Blender/Bonsai, third-party Rhino MCPs, Figma) to an appendix.

false_assumptions.why_false: Discourse search for 'AI' returns substring matches; a search for 'MCP' returns several AI-agent topics from 2026.

false_assumptions.why_false: Both statements are by scottd (Scott Davidson), a McNeel admin, in thread 223330: he states McNeel's intent and reports his own usage.
false_assumptions.correction: Treat them as vendor staff statements, not community sentiment. Remove them from principle 13's evidence for user demand, and label the token figure as a McNeel staff anecdote.

false_assumptions.why_false: Those counts covered page 1 only. Discourse reports 28 participants (76 posts) and 42 participants (100 posts).
false_assumptions.correction: Use participant_count from the topic JSON, excluding McNeel staff (scottd and theoutside in 211382; Japhy in 216046).

false_assumptions.claim: In principle 15, the 'door altered' fidelity complaint is evidence about RhinoAI renders.
false_assumptions.why_false: In thread 223330 the altered front door, impossible chair legs and stray lamp were pointed out in a Krita AI Diffusion image, not a RhinoAI output.
false_assumptions.correction: Attribute it to Krita AI. The RhinoAI-specific issue in that thread is a mis-scaled ('sitcom version') model built from a guessed sketch plan.

false_assumptions.claim: Autodesk's Revit 2027 MCP release post documents separate Write and Experimental installers, and writes are undoable.
false_assumptions.why_false: The release post lists only seven read tools and no write tools. The installers come from a later post, which advises backing up and does not claim undo.
false_assumptions.correction: Cite blog.autodesk.io/revit-mcp-server-update/ (29 Sep 2026) for the installers and Revit 2027.2. Attribute 'undoable' to AEC Magazine's interview quote.

verdict: Conditional pass. The tooling half is accurate and ready to act on: the MCP revision, the headless .mcp.json risk, Node, gpt-image limits, Figma, Revit MCP, Buildner dates, GitHub lockdown and rhino-gh-mcp all check out. The sentiment half still fails corroboration. McNeel staff statements are counted as user voices, and the voice counts are 2 to 5 times too low. The 'no AI topics on the Ladybug forum' claim is false and missed GPL Ladybug/Honeybee MCPs and an MIT Design Explorer. The search tallies do not reproduce. The round-2 gaps are mostly closed. Build from the do-this-first list now. Treat every sentiment principle as an unverified hypothesis until the attributions are fixed and the 3 Nov log has an owner and an official-API method.
